# Chicago Education Digest
_Aug 17 – Aug 31, 2026_

> Covering: K-12 Education & Schools · Board of Education & Governance

## K-12 Curriculum & Instruction

The new school year has commenced in Chicago Public Schools, with students returning to classrooms across the district. As the academic year begins, attention is being paid to operational considerations such as classroom resources and enrollment figures, which can influence the delivery of instruction.

Discussions around specific curriculum and instructional practices have also come to the forefront. Candidates for the upcoming elected school board have expressed varied perspectives regarding the integration and use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) within classrooms. Additionally, a Congressional committee has requested information from Chicago Public Schools concerning its gender policies and curriculum. These developments point to ongoing conversations and potential policy considerations related to educational content and methods.

## Students & School Life

The new school year for Chicago Public Schools students began this past week, with widespread reporting on their return to classrooms. A prominent theme across much of the coverage was the ongoing budget uncertainty facing the district, including concerns about state funding and its potential impact on school operations. The Chicago Board of Education held its first meeting since students returned, where budget issues remained a central topic of discussion.

Alongside the start of the academic year, several specific student support policies and related developments were reported. Chicago Public Schools announced a new policy aimed at simplifying enrollment and access to support services for students experiencing homelessness. The district also successfully recovered millions in federal grants that had been previously withheld in connection with its Black Student Success Plan. Separately, a House of Representatives committee is reportedly investigating the legality of CPS policies supporting transgender students. One report also noted the return of students amidst existing challenges such as low proficiency rates and underutilized school facilities.

## School Safety

As Chicago Public Schools students returned to classrooms for the new academic year, a notable development in school safety emerged from the West Side. Community members have been instrumental in expanding the "Whole School Safety plan," indicating a collaborative approach to enhancing student well-being and security within schools.

This expansion highlights an ongoing effort to integrate community perspectives and involvement into safety strategies. While the broader return to school also brought discussions on topics such as classroom resource allocation and enrollment figures, the specific focus on safety in recent reports centered on these community-led initiatives to strengthen the existing safety framework.

## Budget & Finance

Chicago Public Schools (CPS) recently secured millions in federal funding that had been previously withheld. This recovery stems from a lawsuit settlement, specifically related to the district's Black Student Success Plan. Multiple reports confirm that CPS has successfully regained these federal grants, which were withheld by a previous administration.

Despite this recent financial gain, the district continues to face budget uncertainty as students return to school. This ongoing financial landscape is a prominent topic among candidates vying for Chicago school board president, highlighting its importance in future district leadership and policy discussions.

## Board of Education & Governance

The transition to a fully elected Chicago Board of Education remains a prominent topic, with developments in the race for the first elected board president. Candidate Jennifer Custer withdrew from the presidential race this week. Another candidate, Victor Henderson, publicly addressed past allegations. Media outlets have introduced the remaining candidates, detailing their stances on key issues such as the CPS budget and the integration of artificial intelligence in classrooms. An upcoming town hall is scheduled to provide a platform for candidates to discuss their visions for the district.

Concurrently, the current appointed Board of Education convened for its first meeting since students returned to school, with budget concerns noted as a significant ongoing issue. The board also advanced a new policy designed to streamline enrollment and support services for students experiencing homelessness. Broader discussions in the news highlighted existing challenges within Chicago Public Schools, including student proficiency levels and the utilization of school facilities, providing context for the incoming elected board's future responsibilities.

## Equity & Civil Rights

Recent developments in Chicago Public Schools highlight both external scrutiny and internal leadership shifts concerning equity and civil rights. A U.S. House of Representatives committee has initiated an investigation into CPS policies supporting transgender students, specifically requesting information on gender policies and curriculum, and raising questions about parental notification regarding "gender affirmation." Concurrently, CPS successfully recovered millions in federal grants that had been withheld in connection with its Black Student Success Plan, indicating a resolution regarding funding for this key equity initiative.

In other news impacting the district's future governance, incumbent school board member Jennifer Custer has withdrawn from the race to become the first elected CPS board president. This development will shape the field of candidates for the upcoming election for the new leadership structure of the school board.
